title: De novo design of proteases - Nature Biotechnology
text:
De novo design of proteases remains particularly challenging because of the biochemical complexity of their catalytic sites. Reporting in two separate papers in Nature, Choi and colleagues and Chen and colleagues describe the de novo design of cysteine proteases and metalloproteases using machine learning-based tools.Choi and colleagues used a version of the RoseTTAFold diffusion model that was optimized for designing enzyme active sites and protein–protein interactions, termed RoseTTAFold Diffusion 2 for Molecular Interfaces (RFD2-MI). The authors generated 69 computational designs of cysteine proteases and found that 13 were catalytically active and cleaved their target peptide sequences. Structural studies revealed the presence of an aspartate–histidine–cysteine catalytic triad and showed that the designed enzymes adopted folds distinct from those of natural cysteine proteases. Further studies confirmed that the designed proteases were enzymatically active in mammalian cells.
